This landing page provides a human-readable summary of the data points that link to this {entity}. The data included in this summary reflect only those data points used in the MMM Portal. Click the Open in Linked Data Browser on button on the Export tab to view the complete set of classes and properties linked to this record.

To cite this record, use its url. You can use also use the url to return directly to the record at any time.
instancePageGeneral.repetition:
Repetition of data

The same or similar data may appear within a single data field multiple times. This repetition occurs due to the merging of multiple records from different datasets to create the MMM record.

aboutThePortalPartOne:
About the project

The ERC Starting Grant project WRITE – New Forms of Calligraphy in China: A Contemporary Culture Mirror (GA n. 949645) is a major research initiative that explores how evolving forms of calligraphy in contemporary China are reshaping cultural identity. With its growing presence in contemporary art, WRITE systematically analyses these transformations as both artistic expressions and cultural phenomena.

Building on the extensive research conducted within WRITE, the WenDAng project aims to create the first open-access semantic digital archive dedicated to these emerging forms of Chinese calligraphy. WenDAng can be understood as the digital extension of WRITE: it uses the heterogeneous data collected through the research project to offer a centralised platform for conservation, exploration, analysis, and public engagement.

Grounded in Digital Humanities, WenDAng leverages computational tools to preserve, analyse, represent, and visualise the findings gathered through WRITE, while maintaining a critical awareness of the cultural significance of the objects studied. This methodology not only provides new perspectives on contemporary calligraphy, but also redefines how knowledge about it is generated and disseminated.

What you can find in WenDAng

Through WenDAng, users can explore artworks from the four WRITE collections - Visual Arts, Performing Arts, Graffiti Art, and Decorative and Applied Arts. The archive also includes artists, calligraphers, exhibitions, and other entities relevant to the project.

Another important section of the archive is dedicated to so-called “Calli-Writing” units. Within an artwork, a Calli-Writing unit is a content unit that features elements of calligraphy and/or writing, whether in the form of meaningful writing, a set of signs, and/or a set of lines.

The archive is designed not only as a catalogue, but also as a research tool that enables the analysis of complex relationships among these entities.
aboutThePortalPartTwo:
At the core of WenDAng is the WRITE ontology, which enables the representation of both tangible and intangible aspects of this important cultural, artistic, linguistic, and social phenomenon. Together with a dedicated thesaurus, the ontology helps bridge existing gaps in the representation of traditional and contemporary expressions of calligraphy and art.

The WRITE ontology can be consulted here.

The WRITE thesaurus can be consulted here.

To consult the detailed documentation of the WenDAng project, visit the project documentation.
